verses.restored: Sons of prophets said to Elisha, Look, place where we dwell before you is too narrow for us.
Let us go, please, to Jordan and take from there each man one beam, and make for ourselves there a place to dwell. He said, Go.
One said, Please be willing and go with your servants. He said, I will go.
He went with them, and they came to Jordan and cut trees.
It was, when one was felling the beam, that iron fell into water. He cried and said, Ah, my lord! And it was borrowed.
Man of Divine said, Where did it fall? He showed him place. He cut a stick, threw it there, and made iron float.
He said, Lift it for yourself. He stretched out his hand and took it.
King of Aram was fighting against Israel, and he counseled with his servants, saying, At such and such place shall be my camp.
Man of Divine sent to king of Israel, saying, Guard yourself from passing this place, for there Arameans are descending.
King of Israel sent to place man of Divine told him and warned him about, and he guarded himself there, not once or twice.
Heart of king of Aram stormed over this matter. He called his servants and said to them, Will you not tell me who among us is for king of Israel?
One of his servants said, No, my lord king; but Elisha prophet who is in Israel tells king of Israel words you speak in chamber of your lying down.
He said, Go and see where he is, and I will send and take him. It was told to him, saying, Look, he is in Dothan.
He sent there horses, chariots, and a heavy force; they came by night and surrounded city.
Servant of man of Divine rose early and went out, and look, a force surrounded city with horses and chariots. His young man said to him, Ah, my lord, what shall we do?
He said, Do not fear, for more are those with us than those with them.
Elisha prayed and said, YHWH, please open his eyes so he may see. YHWH opened eyes of young man, and he saw, and look, mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.
They came down to him, and Elisha prayed to YHWH and said, Please strike this nation with blindness/confusion. He struck them with blindness/confusion according to word of Elisha.
Elisha said to them, This is not the way and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to man whom you seek. He led them to Samaria.
It was, when they came to Samaria, that Elisha said, YHWH, open eyes of these so they may see. YHWH opened their eyes, and they saw, and look, they were in midst of Samaria.
King of Israel said to Elisha when he saw them, Shall I strike, shall I strike, my father?
He said, You shall not strike. Would you strike those whom you captured with your sword and bow? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their lord.
He prepared for them a great feast; they ate and drank, and he sent them away, and they went to their lord. Bands of Aram did not continue to enter land of Israel.
It was after this that Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his camp, went up, and besieged Samaria.
There was great famine in Samaria. Look, they besieged it until head of donkey was for eighty silver and fourth of a qab of dove's dung/seedpods for five silver.
It was, when king of Israel was passing upon wall, that a woman cried to him, saying, Save, my lord king!
He said, If YHWH does not save you, from where shall I save you—from threshing floor or winepress?
King said to her, What is for you? She said, This woman said to me, Give your son and we will eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.
So we cooked my son and ate him. I said to her on next day, Give your son and we will eat him, but she hid her son.
It was, when king heard words of woman, that he tore his garments while passing on wall, and people saw, and look, sackcloth was beneath upon his flesh.
He said, Thus may Divine do to me and thus add, if head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains upon him today.

Elisha was sitting in his house, and elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man from before him. Before messenger came to him, he said to elders, Do you see that this son of murderer has sent to remove my head? See, when messenger comes, shut door and press him with door. Is not sound of feet of his lord behind him?
While he was still speaking with them, look, messenger came down to him, and king said, Look, this evil is from YHWH; why should I wait for YHWH any longer?

translation_notes: The sons of prophets need more living space and organize collective labor. Spiritual community still requires housing, tools, land access, and practical planning.
The lost axe head matters because it was borrowed. The small miracle centers liability, poverty, and restoration of another person's property rather than spectacle.
Military intelligence attributed to Elisha protects Israel but also turns prophetic knowledge into a wartime asset; this must not authorize surveillance claims or leader omniscience.
The servant's opened eyes are a reassurance scene, not proof that every danger is secretly surrounded by supernatural force or that fear is irrational.
The Hebrew term in verses 18 and 20 may imply dazzlement, confusion, or impaired perception rather than ordinary blindness. It must not support stigma against blind people.
Elisha forbids execution of the captured Arameans and commands food and water. Feeding enemies interrupts a cycle of killing and produces a period without raids.
The later royal siege shows the truce did not permanently end interstate war. One act of mercy is still ethically meaningful even when it does not guarantee lasting peace.
The famine prices portray extreme scarcity; the precise term translated dove's dung may refer to a plant or seedpod and requires lexical audit.
The two mothers' story is siege atrocity and starvation trauma. The woman whose son was eaten is not morally responsible for conditions created by war and famine.
The king redirects grief and rage toward Elisha. Leaders must not scapegoat prophets, civilians, minorities, or critics for systemic catastrophe.
safety_note: Do not use the vision or blindness scene to stigmatize disability, claim supernatural surveillance, or manipulate frightened people. Do not blame starving parents for siege atrocities. Center borrowed-property restoration, fear met with reassurance, prisoners fed rather than killed, and political responsibility for famine and war.
